pk.context: 25 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: A JAK inhibitor with active metabolites; their combined exposure rises up to 1.9-fold in renal impairment.

clues.text: A high-fat meal has no clinically relevant effect, and about 97% is bound to protein, mostly albumin. It is metabolized mainly by CYP3A4 and to a lesser extent by CYP2C9.
A phosphate salt with a molecular weight of 306.4 for the active moiety, soluble in aqueous buffers across a pH range of 1 to 8.
Approved under an NDA as 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 mg tablets, dosed twice daily.
No boxed warning. Bruising, dizziness, headache and diarrhea are the most common nonhematologic reactions.
Intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis, polycythemia vera with inadequate response to hydroxyurea, and steroid-refractory acute or chronic graft-versus-host disease.
Inhibits JAK1 and JAK2, which mediate cytokine and growth factor signaling important for hematopoiesis and immune function.
The generic name begins with R and has eleven letters.
